Clean growth measurements (main growthcleanr function)

Source: R/child_clean.R
cleangrowth.Rd

growthcleanr flags implausible values in longitudinal anthropometric measurements – weight, height/length, and head circumference – for children and adults. growthcleanr is specifically designed to evaluate electronic health record data for outpatients. It does not delete or edit your data. It returns your data with an added exclude column labeling each row either "Include" or an exclusion code naming why it was set aside. Each subject is cleaned independently, using that subject's own measurement trajectory over time, so splitting, subsetting, or batching the data does not change any subject's result.

The default input is one row per measurement in long format with columns subjid, param, agedays, sex, and measurement (plus an optional per-row id); semi-wide and wide layouts are also accepted (see input_format). You can use date of birth and visit date instead of agedays. Most runs need only the input-column arguments; see "Arguments at a glance" under Details for how the rest are grouped.

New to growthcleanr? Start with vignette("new-start-here"). To check that growthcleanr is reading your columns, sex coding, and parameters correctly before a full run, use gc_runtrial on a sample of your data. See vignette("output") for the returned columns and vignette("configuration") for the full argument index. For ready-to-run scripts covering common setups, see vignette("example-scripts").

Usage

cleangrowth(
  data = NULL,
  subjid = NULL,
  param = NULL,
  agedays = NULL,
  sex = NULL,
  measurement = NULL,
  piv.z.wt.high = 22,
  piv.z.ht.low.young = -25,
  piv.z.ht.low.old = -15,
  piv.z.ht.high = 8,
  piv.z.hc.low = -15,
  piv.z.hc.high = 15,
  error.load.mincount = 2,
  error.load.threshold = 0.5,
  sd.recenter = NA,
  cf_rescue = "standard",
  cf_detail = FALSE,
  corr_detail = FALSE,
  recenter_detail = FALSE,
  qm_detail = FALSE,
  ref.data.path = "",
  log.path = NA,
  parallel = FALSE,
  cores = NULL,
  quietly = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  adult_cutpoint = 20,
  adult_permissiveness = "looser",
  adult_scale_max_lbs = Inf,
  ewma_window = 15,
  adult_overrides = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  dob = NULL,
  visit_date = NULL,
  age_source = NULL,
  date_order = NULL,
  sex_coding = .gc_default_sex_coding,
  param_coding = NULL,
  carry_through = TRUE,
  input_format = "long",
  output_format = NULL,
  semiwide_cols = NULL,
  widened_emit = "exclude",
  wide_cols = NULL,
  max_blocks = 25,
  internal_detail = FALSE,
  ref_tables = NULL,
  tri_exclude = FALSE,
  debug = FALSE,
  full_detail = FALSE,
  unit_error_range = TRUE,
  display_gc_id = FALSE,
  exclude_detail = FALSE,
  mean_ht = TRUE,
  batch_size = 5000,
  length.adjust = FALSE,
  checkpoint = TRUE,
  checkpoint_dir = NULL,
  checkpoint_size = 5000,
  checkpoint_resume = FALSE,
  keep_checkpoints = TRUE,
  log_file = NULL,
  .checkpoint_driven = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

Optional data.frame or data.table containing the input measurements. When supplied, subjid, param, agedays, sex, measurement, and id are interpreted as column-name strings (defaulting to the canonical names). When NULL (the default), the function uses the legacy vector-style API.

subjid

Subject identifier. In data-frame style, a column name (default "subjid"). In vector style, a vector of subject identifiers, one entry per measurement row (repeated across a subject's rows).

param

Measurement parameter. In data-frame style, a column name (default "param"); in vector style, a vector. Recognized values are "WEIGHTKG", "WEIGHTLBS", "HEIGHTCM", "HEIGHTIN", "LENGTHCM", "LENGTHIN", "HEADCM", and "HEADIN". Matching is case-insensitive and whitespace-trimmed, but the names must be spelled out: there are deliberately no built-in abbreviations, so a short label such as "wt", "ht", or "hc" is not assumed to be a growthcleanr parameter because it might be a statistical sample weight or something similar. Declare any non-canonical label with param_coding. Unrecognized params are set aside as Exclude-Not-GC-Param (with a warning); the value is preserved.

Units and length/height handling: imperial parameters ("WEIGHTLBS", "HEIGHTIN", "LENGTHIN", "HEADIN") are converted to metric during calculation. By default, linear measurements under 2 years are evaluated as length and at 2 years (day 730) and older as height, regardless of whether they are input using a LENGTH or HEIGHT parameter; in children whose data are consistent with prematurity or small-for-gestational age (SGA) and who receive an assigned gestational age for cleaning purposes, that gestational age is used to determine an estimated corrected age, and this corrected age is used to determine default linear growth handling. This default behavior can be changed with length.adjust = TRUE. Full detail is in vignette("wrapper"), section "Length vs. height handling".

agedays

Age in days at each measurement. In data-frame style, a column name (default "agedays"). In vector style, a numeric vector. May be omitted if age is supplied instead as dob + visit_date (see age_source); when an agedays column is present it takes precedence over dates by default. Cleaning uses whole days: a fractional age is rounded down (1435.4 is day 1435; -0.5 is day -1) for all cleaning, but the submitted value is returned in the output agedays column (the whole-day value is available as gc_internal_agedays under internal_detail).

sex

Subject sex. In data-frame style, a column name (default "sex"). In vector style, a vector. By default 0, "m", "b", "male", or "boy" are read as male and 1, "f", "g", "female", or "girl" as female (case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed); override with sex_coding. On pediatric rows, values matching neither list (and blank/NA) are set aside as Exclude-Missing-Info (with a warning). A sex column is always required, but the sex column value may be blank or NA for adults (ages at or above adult_cutpoint): the adult algorithm does not require a valid value in the sex column, but when available, it is used in the Evil Twins step and in calculating whether a value falls in the unit error range. A 1=male/2=female coding is detected and rejected with an informative error (growthcleanr reads 1 as female), so it cannot silently misclassify data; pass sex_coding = list(male = 1, female = 2) if that is your coding. If there is more than one subject and every value is 1, which could be all-female 0/1 data or all-male 1/2 data, it is read as female with a prominent warning (the run continues); pass an explicit sex_coding or code sex as F to remove the warning.

measurement

Recorded measurement. In data-frame style, a column name (default "measurement"). In vector style, a numeric vector. Weight must be in kilograms (kg), and linear measurements in centimeters (cm), unless param is "WEIGHTLBS", "HEIGHTIN", "LENGTHIN", or "HEADIN". Text or factor values are converted to numbers for cleaning (values that are not numbers are set aside as Exclude-Missing-Info) and are returned as submitted.

piv.z.wt.high

Upper unrecentered CSD z-score cutoff for WEIGHTKG (all ages). Weights with sd.orig > piv.z.wt.high are excluded as hard limits (Exclude-Hard-Limit). Defaults to 22.

piv.z.ht.low.young

Lower unrecentered CSD z-score cutoff for HEIGHTCM under one year of age. Heights with sd.orig < piv.z.ht.low.young are excluded as hard limits (Exclude-Hard-Limit). Defaults to -25.

piv.z.ht.low.old

Lower unrecentered CSD z-score cutoff for HEIGHTCM at or above one year. Heights with sd.orig < piv.z.ht.low.old are excluded as hard limits (Exclude-Hard-Limit). Defaults to -15.

piv.z.ht.high

Upper unrecentered CSD z-score cutoff for HEIGHTCM (all ages). Heights with sd.orig > piv.z.ht.high are excluded as hard limits (Exclude-Hard-Limit). Defaults to 8 (tighter than the weight upper limit).

piv.z.hc.low

Lower unrecentered CSD z-score cutoff for HEADCM (all ages). Head-circumference values with sd.orig < piv.z.hc.low are excluded as hard limits (Exclude-Hard-Limit). Defaults to -15.

piv.z.hc.high

Upper unrecentered CSD z-score cutoff for HEADCM (all ages). Head-circumference values with sd.orig > piv.z.hc.high are excluded as hard limits (Exclude-Hard-Limit). Defaults to 15.

error.load.mincount

Minimum number of real errors (exclusions other than Exclude-Identical, Exclude-Extraneous, Exclude-CF, Exclude-Missing-Info, and Exclude-HC-Out-of-Range) required per (subject, param) group before Child Step 21 Error Load is evaluated for that group. Defaults to 2. Unlike 2.2.3, a high error load for one parameter can no longer result in the exclusion of the other parameter's values.

error.load.threshold

Error ratio threshold for Child Step 21. The ratio is n_errors / (n_errors + n_includes) computed per (subject, param) group, where n_errors and n_includes leave out the codes listed under error.load.mincount. If the ratio strictly exceeds this threshold (and at least error.load.mincount real errors are present), all remaining Include rows for that (subject, param) group are excluded with Exclude-Traj-Uneval. Defaults to 0.5.

sd.recenter

Recentering medians. One of:

NA (default)

Use the built-in reference file (rcfile-resmoothed.csv.gz). (In 2.x, NA derived medians from the input data for larger datasets; that option was removed.)

"none"

No recentering: the recentered scores equal the reference scores (tbc.sd = sd.orig).

A data.table or data.frame

Your own medians, with columns param, sex, agedays, and rcmedian.sd (a median column named sd.median is also accepted). The table must have exactly one median per param, sex, and agedays, and a median for every param, sex, and agedays of the child measurements to be cleaned; otherwise growthcleanr stops and reports the problem.

The 2.x options "nhanes" and "derive" were removed and stop with an error. See vignette("recentering").

cf_rescue

CF rescue mode for the child algorithm. One of:

"standard"

(Default) Decide each identical-value string on its last copy in the string; the whole string is rescued or excluded together. When the last CF has a next included value, rescue if cf_deltaz + cf_nextz <= 1 and cf_deltaz <= 1.5; when it has no next value, rescue by age (cf_deltaz <= 0.5 if agedays < 13*365.25, else cf_deltaz <= 1). cf_deltaz is the absolute difference between the value's z-score before recentering and the z-score of the value that was copied. See vignette("cf-rescue").

"none"

All potential carried-forward values are excluded. A value is detected as carried forward when it exactly equals the measurement on the subject's previous measurement day and that day has only one measurement for the parameter (see vignette("cf-rescue")).

"all"

No potential carried-forward values are excluded at this step; they are evaluated by the later steps like any other value.

cf_detail

Logical. If TRUE, add six carried-forward (CF) columns to the output: cf_status (each row's CF role, e.g. "Orig", "CF-R" (rescued), "CF-NR" (not rescued), "Not-CF", or "Adult"), cf_deltaz and cf_nextz (the z-score differences used in the rescue decision), and three design aids for CF-logic development (imperial, cf_dage_orig, cf_dage_next). Each column and value is defined in vignette("output"), section 4, and the rescue rule in vignette("cf-rescue"). Defaults to FALSE.

corr_detail

Logical. If TRUE, include corr_val and corr_pt columns in the output. corr_val labels each value "Corrected" (its gestational-age-corrected z-score differs from the uncorrected one), "Uncorrected", or "Adult" (adult row). corr_pt labels each subject "Corrected" (the subject has at least one corrected value), "Uncorrected", or "Adult". Defaults to FALSE.

recenter_detail

Logical. If TRUE, include the recentered CSD z-score columns in the output: tbc.sd (the recentered z used throughout the child algorithm), ctbc.sd (its gestational-age-corrected counterpart), and rcmedian.sd (the per-row recentering median that was subtracted). This is specialized output for a related tool in development (see vignette("output"), section 5b). The three columns are a subset of what debug surfaces. Child rows only; adult rows receive NA. Defaults to FALSE. Also turned on by full_detail = TRUE.

qm_detail

Logical. If TRUE, emit the child-algorithm per-step eligibility flags (qm_elig_c_cf, qm_elig_c_hardlimit, qm_elig_c_eviltwins, qm_elig_c_trajextreme, qm_elig_extraneous, qm_elig_c_traj, qm_elig_c_absdiff, qm_elig_c_pair, qm_elig_c_single, qm_elig_c_trajuneval): one logical column per reported cleaning step marking the rows that were eligible for (in scope of) that step – the denominator against which that step's exclusions are measured. Child rows only; NA on adult rows. Used for calculations in a related package currently in development. Not used in cleaning; typically paired with exclude_detail = TRUE so downstream code can derive which step excluded each row. Additive, write-only (does not affect any exclusion decision), and off by default. Must be requested explicitly – it is NOT turned on by full_detail. Defaults to FALSE.

ref.data.path

Path to reference data. If not supplied, the reference files included with growthcleanr are used.

log.path

Deprecated; supplying it gives a warning. Use log_file instead. (It still writes per-batch log files in parallel, non-quiet runs.)

parallel

Determines if function runs in parallel. Defaults to FALSE. See vignette("large-datasets") and "Large datasets: run in parallel and save progress" in vignette("example-scripts").

cores

Number of parallel worker processes to use when parallel = TRUE. NULL (the default) auto-detects min(8, parallel::detectCores() - 1) – capped at 8 because growthcleanr's per-worker setup overhead makes more workers than that counterproductive. Pass a positive whole number to override; a value above the machine's core count is reduced to it (extra workers only oversubscribe, and an extreme value would stall the run spawning workers). Ignored when parallel = FALSE. (Replaces the former num.batches argument.)

quietly

Controls progress output. With the default quietly = FALSE, growthcleanr prints a minimal progress view: a "cleaning in progress" line, an X/Y batch (or checkpoint) counter, and the end-of-run cleaning summary. Set quietly = TRUE to turn off the progress lines and the summary. Warnings still appear, as does the one-time note shown when cleangrowth() is called with vectors (the 2.x style); that note is a message, so suppressMessages() will silence it. For the detailed per-step view, use verbose instead. Defaults to FALSE.

verbose

When TRUE, prints the detailed view: the milestone lines (preprocessing, per-batch cleaning child/adult) plus granular per-step diagnostics (pre-filter counts, EWMA/SDE iteration counts, etc.). Implies quietly = FALSE. Intended for development and debugging. Defaults to FALSE.

adult_cutpoint

Age in years, between 18 and 20, describing ages when the pediatric algorithm should not be applied (< adult_cutpoint), and the adult algorithm should apply (>= adult_cutpoint). Numbers outside this range are changed to the closest number within the range, with a warning. Defaults to 20. growthcleanr does not change this value based on your data (so each subject is cleaned independently of the rest of the dataset); if it is left at the default and every measurement with a known age is at age 18 years or older, a warning suggests setting adult_cutpoint = 18 to clean those 18-to-20-year-olds with the adult algorithm instead of the pediatric one.

adult_permissiveness

Permissiveness level for the adult algorithm: "loosest", "looser" (default), "tighter", or "tightest" (case and surrounding spaces are ignored). Sets defaults for all adult PIV limits, EWMA caps, height bands, etc. To change one or a few of those settings without switching preset, use adult_overrides. For the intended use of each level and its preset values, see Section 1D of vignette("configuration"). For a ready-to-run script, see "Data that includes adults" in vignette("example-scripts").

adult_scale_max_lbs

Physical scale upper limit in pounds for adult weight data (replaces 2.2.3's weight_cap, which was in kg). Weights within +/-0.1 kg of the cap are excluded if they are more than 50 kg different from their expected value, or if all of the subject's weights (at least two) are the same value at the cap. Defaults to Inf.

ewma_window

Used by both the child and adult algorithms. Number of measurements on each side included in the exponentially weighted moving average (EWMA) weighting window. Defaults to 15.

adult_overrides

Optional named list overriding individual adult permissiveness settings (those set by adult_permissiveness), e.g. list(overall_ht_min = 120, allow_ht_gain = FALSE). Each named value replaces the preset value for that setting; unnamed or unrecognized names are an error. Applies to adult rows only. The recognized names are the adult settings listed in vignette("configuration") (Section 1D). Defaults to NULL (use the preset for every setting).

id

Row identifier. Optional but recommended. In data-frame style, a column name (default "id"); in vector style, a vector of row ids. If id is absent / NULL / contains NA / is not unique, a warning is issued and sequential integer ids (1:N in input row order) are auto-generated for internal use. The user's original id (whatever was supplied - even if NA or duplicated) is preserved in the output id column so callers can map results back to their data. To see the id that growthcleanr actually used internally, set display_gc_id = TRUE (or full_detail = TRUE); the output then includes a gc_internal_id column equal to the user's id when no regen was needed, or the auto-generated 1:N when a regen occurred. For stable row identifiers, supply a unique per-row id; a per-subject or per-encounter identifier is not a valid id for this purpose. For semi-wide/wide input with long output, the subject, sex and age columns are returned under the user's own names (for wide input, the age prefix), and the id identifies an input row, not a measurement: it is returned under its own column name (repeated on each measurement from that row), and growthcleanr's per-measurement number is returned as gc_internal_id; with no id column there is no id column in that output. An id column named like a column growthcleanr returns (e.g. exclude) comes back as userinput_<name>, with a warning. In semi-wide/wide input the id need not be unique; in semi-wide input it orders a subject's visit rows when the per-measurement ids are assigned (see vignette("wrapper")), and in wide input it does not affect cleaning.

dob

Date of birth (data-frame style only). A column name; the column is class Date or text. Supplied with visit_date to compute agedays as floor(visit_date - dob) in whole days. A subject with more than one distinct dob value is set aside as Exclude-Missing-Info, with a warning. Text dates are accepted in any order-free format – year-first numeric ("2013-03-04", "2013/03/04", "20130304") or English spelled-month ("03mar2013", "15 Mar 2013", "March 15, 2024"); ambiguous numeric day/month dates ("3/4/2013") require date_order. All dob and visit_date values must share one format, the year must be four digits (1900-2099; two-digit years are rejected), and blank/NA yields a missing agedays. A value with no digits (e.g. "N/A", "NULL") is treated as blank, and a few values that are not real dates (e.g. "2013-02-30"; at most 1, or 5\ aside; both are reported in the input warning. More unreadable dates than that stop the run. Numeric date columns (e.g. software date integers from Stata, Excel, etc.) are rejected as ambiguous – convert to text or an R Date first. A lone dob or visit_date supplied alongside an agedays column is parsed and returned only (as gc_internal_dob/gc_internal_visit_date under internal_detail); ages still come from the agedays column unless you set age_source = "dates" to force date-based ages. Default NULL. See "Use dates instead of age in days" in vignette("example-scripts").

visit_date

Visit (measurement) date (data-frame style only). A column name; class Date or text in the same formats as dob. Supplied with dob to compute agedays, or on its own alongside an agedays column purely to be parsed and returned as gc_internal_visit_date (under internal_detail). See dob. Default NULL.

age_source

Which age source to use when resolving agedays: "agedays" (use the agedays column) or "dates" (compute from dob + visit_date). Default NULL auto-resolves: an agedays column is used whenever present, otherwise dob + visit_date are used. Set "dates" to force date-based ages even when an agedays column is also present; that column is then returned as submitted, and the ages computed from the dates are returned as gc_internal_agedays.

date_order

Day-vs-month order for ambiguous numeric dob / visit_date values, e.g. "3/4/2013" (data-frame style only). "dmy" reads day-month-year, "mdy" reads month-day-year; applied uniformly to the whole run. Default NULL accepts only the order-free formats (year-first numeric and English spelled-month) and errors on numeric day/month dates, so an ambiguous order is never guessed. growthcleanr never auto-detects the order.

sex_coding

Named list with elements male and female, each a vector of the codes (numbers or strings) that denote that sex in your data. Defaults to list(male = c(0, "m", "b", "male", "boy"), female = c(1, "f", "g", "female", "girl")). Matching is case-insensitive and whitespace-trimmed. Supplying your own table replaces the defaults wholesale (include any standard codes you also use) and suppresses the 1/2 guard. Errors if a code is listed under both sexes. See "Set your sex coding (including 1 = male, 2 = female)" in vignette("example-scripts").

param_coding

Optional named list mapping your parameter labels to growthcleanr's canonical parameters, e.g. list(WEIGHTKG = c("WT", "Weight"), HEIGHTIN = "HT"). Names must be canonical parameters (WEIGHTKG, WEIGHTLBS, HEIGHTCM, HEIGHTIN, LENGTHCM, LENGTHIN, HEADCM, HEADIN); values are the labels to remap (case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed). This is the only way to have a non-canonical label recognized (there are no built-in abbreviations), and also how you declare that a remapped column is imperial (map it to WEIGHTLBS/HEIGHTIN/LENGTHIN/HEADIN); otherwise a remapped label defaults to its metric target. Errors if a name is not canonical or a label maps to two parameters. Default NULL. See "Use your own measurement-type labels (WT / HT / HC)" in vignette("example-scripts").

carry_through

Logical (data-frame style only). If TRUE (default), any column in data that growthcleanr does not consume as a role column (i.e. anything other than the resolved subjid, param, agedays, sex, measurement, and id columns) is carried through and returned appended after the growthcleanr output columns, in its original input order and values. dob/visit_date are carried through this way (so submitted dates are echoed back). A carried column whose name matches a column growthcleanr returns in this run (for example exclude, when re-cleaning growthcleanr output) is returned under the name userinput_<name>, with a warning; names of growthcleanr columns not returned in the run are left alone. FALSE restores the prior behavior of dropping all non-role columns. With semi-wide or wide output the user's columns return structurally (the submitted table is the output base), so TRUE keeps every column and FALSE keeps only the role, id, and parameter value columns. With semi-wide or wide input and long output, the other columns (including dob/visit_date; in wide input, not the per-block columns) are repeated on each measurement from their row.

input_format

Shape of data: "long" (default; one row per measurement), "semi_wide" (one row per visit: a subjid, an age source, a sex, and one column per parameter), or "wide" (one row per subject: a subjid, a sex, and repeated observation blocks marked by a _N suffix – agedays_1, wt_1, ht_1, agedays_2, ...). Semi-wide and wide are reshaped to long before cleaning, so results match submitting the same measurements in long format; both require the data-frame style. Map your own column names with semiwide_cols/wide_cols. For ready-to-run scripts, see "Semi-wide data (one row per visit)" and "Wide data (one row per subject)" in vignette("example-scripts").

Length/height in non-long formats. Customized recumbent-length vs standing-height handling is a long-format-only feature: semi-wide and wide always use default handling (values under 2 years treated as recumbent length, 2 years and over as standing height, using estimated corrected age for children whose data are consistent with prematurity or small-for-gestational age (SGA) and who receive an assigned gestational age for cleaning purposes). So length.adjust = TRUE is rejected for these formats, and a LENGTHCM/LENGTHIN value at any age gets default handling, the same as in long input with length.adjust = FALSE. See length.adjust and vignette("wrapper"), section "Length vs. height handling".

output_format

Shape of the returned results: "long", "semi_wide", or "wide". Default NULL mirrors input_format, so semi-wide input returns semi-wide output and wide input returns wide output. Re-widened output returns the submitted table itself – every column untouched, one row per input row – with the growthcleanr columns named in widened_emit inserted immediately right of the value column they describe (exclude_wt_kg for semi-wide, exclude_wt_1 for wide). It requires the matching input format (growthcleanr cannot infer visit rows or observation blocks from a different shape); checkpointed runs are supported. Choose output_format = "long" for the full per-measurement result table, which can be merged back onto the source data by subjid/param/agedays.

semiwide_cols

Named list/vector mapping growthcleanr parameter names to the columns holding their values in semi-wide input, e.g. list(WEIGHTKG = "wt_kg", HEIGHTCM = "ht_cm", HEADCM = "head_cm"). Recognized names are WEIGHTKG, HEIGHTCM, LENGTHCM, HEADCM, WEIGHTLBS, HEIGHTIN, LENGTHIN, and HEADIN (imperial/length variants are converted downstream). If NULL (default), columns literally named as recognized parameters are used; at least one recognized parameter column must be present. The restriction rejecting LENGTHCM/LENGTHIN for children 2 years and older (described under input_format) applies. Only used when input_format = "semi_wide".

widened_emit

Character vector naming the growthcleanr output columns to add to re-widened output (semi-wide or wide); default "exclude". Any per-measurement output column may be named (e.g. "bin_exclude", "exclude_detailed", "unit_error_range", "measurement", "agedays"), and a column whose own switch was not enabled is an error. Used when output_format is "semi_wide" or "wide". How the added columns are named (e.g. exclude_wt_kg) is described in vignette("wrapper"), sections "Output format: semi-wide" and "Output format: wide".

wide_cols

Named list/vector mapping growthcleanr parameter names to the column-name prefixes holding their values in wide input, e.g. list(WEIGHTKG = "wt", HEIGHTCM = "ht", HEADCM = "hc") for columns wt_1, wt_2, ht_1, .... You choose the prefix; growthcleanr requires the _N block suffix and discovers the blocks from it. Recognized names are as for semiwide_cols, and the same length-at-2-years restriction (see input_format) applies. If NULL (default), prefixes literally named as recognized parameters are used (WEIGHTKG_1, ...). The age source is a prefix too: agedays names agedays_1, agedays_2, ... (or, on the date route, visit_date names visit_date_1, ... alongside a single patient-level dob column). subjid and sex are patient-level and unsuffixed. Subjects with fewer observations leave their trailing blocks empty; empty cells are dropped. Only used when input_format = "wide".

max_blocks

Highest number of wide observation blocks expected; default 25. Finding more warns (with guidance to raise max_blocks or reshape to long or semi-wide) but still processes every block; an implausible count errors, since it usually means the _N suffixes parsed wrong. Only used when input_format = "wide".

internal_detail

Logical. If TRUE, adds growthcleanr's own working values for the key inputs the user supplied: gc_internal_meas (the measurement gc used – imperial converted to metric and LENGTHCM relabeled; the length.adjust offset is applied only to z-scores, not to this value), gc_internal_param (the parameter label that goes with it), gc_internal_sex (the coerced 0/1 sex), gc_internal_id, and gc_internal_agedays (the whole-day age used for cleaning). The primary measurement, param, agedays, sex, and id columns always return the user's verbatim submission; these report what the algorithm worked with. The imperial conversion is reflected for every row (the adult algorithm applies the same factors), and LENGTHCM is relabeled HEIGHTCM at every age (adult length is cleaned as height); the length.adjust reconciliation is pediatric-only. If a dob and/or visit_date column was supplied, the parsed Date values are also added as gc_internal_dob / gc_internal_visit_date (whether or not the dates drove agedays), showing the interpretation growthcleanr used. Default FALSE. Enabled by full_detail.

ref_tables

Optional. Pre-loaded reference tables from gc_preload_refs. When provided, growthcleanr skips reading the reference files, saving about a second per call. Recommended for repeated calls (e.g., simulation loops). Defaults to NULL (reads files each call).

tri_exclude

Logical. If TRUE, include a tri_exclude column in the output that classifies each row as "Include", "Same-Day" (same-day extraneous values), or "Exclude" (all other exclusions). Defaults to FALSE.

debug

Logical. If TRUE, retain intermediate diagnostic columns in the output instead of trimming to the public columns. Intended for threshold refinement and development, not routine use. Currently surfaces the raw and recentered CSD z-scores captured before cleaning (sd.orig, sd.corr, tbc.sd, ctbc.sd) and the recentered plus/minus perturbation z-scores (tbc.p_plus, tbc.p_minus, ctbc.p_plus, ctbc.p_minus), plus gc_internal_sex (growthcleanr's interpreted 0/1 sex). Adult rows receive NA for the child-only z-score columns. Defaults to FALSE.

full_detail

Logical. Convenience switch: if TRUE, turns on all optional output groups at once (equivalent to cf_detail = TRUE, corr_detail = TRUE, debug = TRUE, tri_exclude = TRUE, display_gc_id = TRUE, recenter_detail = TRUE, internal_detail = TRUE, exclude_detail = TRUE, and mean_ht = TRUE, which is already on by default when the data has adult rows). Defaults to FALSE. Does NOT turn on qm_detail (the quality-measure eligibility flags must be requested explicitly), and does not affect unit_error_range, which is on by default independently.

unit_error_range

Logical. If TRUE (default), include a unit_error_range column: a direction-agnostic flag that is TRUE when a value's magnitude is consistent with a metric/imperial unit-conversion error and the value is not itself within the plausible z = -3 to +3 band. Purely informational – it never affects the exclude decision and is not an exclusion code. Computed only for evaluable rows (Exclude-Missing-Info, Exclude-Not-GC-Param, and Exclude-HC-Out-of-Range rows are FALSE). Real values from people with atypical growth (for example, extremely premature infants, severe obesity, some medical conditions) can fall in the unit-error range. Set FALSE to omit the column.

display_gc_id

Logical. If TRUE, add a gc_internal_id column to the output containing the id that growthcleanr actually used internally: the user's id when it was valid (no regen needed), or the auto-generated 1:N (in input row order) when the user's id was absent / NA / non-unique and growthcleanr had to regenerate. Lets callers recover a reliable per-row key when their input id had problems (the output id column always preserves whatever the user supplied, even if invalid). Defaults to FALSE. Set via full_detail = TRUE alongside the other detail switches. For semi-wide/wide input with long output, gc_internal_id is always returned.

exclude_detail

Logical. If TRUE, add an exclude_detailed column reporting each value's exclusion at the Detailed level: step-level codes that keep the child (-C-) / adult (-A-) algorithm prefix. The default exclude column always reports the consolidated Summary level. Preprocessing codes such as Exclude-Missing-Info are the same in both columns. Defaults to FALSE.

mean_ht

Logical. Include a mean_ht column: the adult algorithm's calculated mean height (cm), computed only from the subject's finally-included heights but populated on all of the subject's adult height rows (an excluded row takes the value of the included height nearest in age). NA for child rows, adult weight rows, and subjects with no included adult height. The column can be used by researchers who want a consistent height for evaluation of body mass index. By default the column is returned when the data has adult rows and omitted otherwise; set TRUE to always return it or FALSE to omit it. For semi-wide or wide output, name it in widened_emit to add it beside the height values.

batch_size

Number of subjects per processing batch. Subjects are never split across batches. Must be a single positive whole number. Defaults to 5000. This is the in-memory granularity (how many subjects are held in RAM at once within a run); it is independent of checkpoint_size, the persist granularity used under checkpointing.

length.adjust

Logical (default FALSE). If TRUE, reconciles how each linear growth measurement was entered with what the reference at that age expects, in both directions: a LENGTHCM value at 2 years or older is z-scored 0.7 cm lower (recumbent to standing) and a HEIGHTCM value under 2 years 0.7 cm higher (standing to recumbent), where 2 years means day 730, the day the reference files switch from length to height; values already in the expected method, and rows with a missing age, are unchanged. The offset is applied only where a value is z-scored: the checks that work in raw centimeters (such as carried-forward detection) and gc_internal_meas use the entered value, and the returned measurement is always the user's verbatim submission. It is pediatric-only (rows at or above adult_cutpoint are not adjusted; adult LENGTHCM/LENGTHIN rows are relabeled as height, so adult length is cleaned as height). Long input only: rejected for input_format "semi_wide"/"wide", which always use default handling. For gestational-age-corrected children with chronological age 2 years or older but corrected age under 2 years, the default presumes recumbent length (the value is z-scored 0.7 cm lower against the standing-height reference), while length.adjust = TRUE uses the label. Full detail (the both-directions table, the exact cutoff, the gestational-age window, and where it runs in preprocessing) is in vignette("wrapper"), section "Length vs. height handling".

checkpoint

Logical (default TRUE). Master switch for checkpointing – cleaning the subjects in checkpoints and writing each finished checkpoint to disk instead of holding the whole dataset in memory at once. Checkpointing substantially speeds up large datasets and prevents the out-of-memory crashes that large in-memory runs can hit (the memory-heavy steps scale super-linearly with the in-memory working set). When TRUE and no checkpoint_dir is given, checkpoints go to an ephemeral per-session temporary directory and are deleted automatically when the run ends, including after an error or interrupt, though not if R itself crashes or is killed (keep_checkpoints is forced FALSE); this only engages when the data exceeds one checkpoint (more than checkpoint_size subjects), since a single checkpoint is the whole dataset in memory and would give no benefit – so small/typical data runs fully in memory with nothing written to disk. Set checkpoint = FALSE to disable checkpointing entirely and never write intermediate data to disk (the escape hatch for environments that forbid any data on disk); if a checkpoint_dir was also supplied it is ignored (with a warning). Supplying checkpoint_dir keeps the files at that location (see below). Very large datasets on a Linux system whose temporary directory is a RAM disk (tmpfs) should pass a checkpoint_dir on a real disk volume; macOS and Windows use disk-backed temporary directories by default.

checkpoint_dir

Optional directory for persistent checkpointed runs. When set, cleangrowth splits subjects into checkpoints of checkpoint_size, cleans each checkpoint, saves its result to a checkpoint_NNNN.rds file in this directory, and combines the checkpoints at the end. Unlike the ephemeral checkpoint = TRUE default, these files persist after the run (subject to keep_checkpoints) and can be resumed: if a run is interrupted, re-running with checkpoint_resume = TRUE skips checkpoints that already have a checkpoint file. The directory is created if it does not exist; use a dedicated directory per dataset/run. When NULL (default), checkpointing – if it engages at all – writes to the ephemeral temporary directory described under checkpoint. Checkpointed results are byte-identical to a single-pass run (each subject's rows stay together in one checkpoint).

checkpoint_size

Number of subjects per checkpoint (one checkpoint_NNNN.rds file per checkpoint). Default 5000. Also the subject count above which the default checkpoint = TRUE engages (temporary folder) when checkpoint_dir is not set. This is the persist granularity and is independent of batch_size (the in-memory granularity within a checkpoint); batch_size < checkpoint_size is allowed. The number of checkpoints is capped at 9999: a checkpoint_size that would exceed the cap is increased to stay within it (with a warning when you set the size; results are not affected). When resuming, use the same checkpoint_size and dataset as the original run.

checkpoint_resume

Logical (default FALSE). Only used when checkpoint_dir is set. When FALSE, the run starts fresh: any checkpoint files already in checkpoint_dir from a prior run are deleted first. When TRUE, existing checkpoint files are reused – checkpoints that already have one are skipped – to resume an interrupted run. When TRUE, you are responsible for using the same dataset, checkpoint_size, and other cleaning arguments as the run that wrote those files; these are not checked, and a mismatch silently mixes results from different settings.

keep_checkpoints

Logical (default TRUE). Only used when checkpoint_dir is set. Controls what happens to the per-checkpoint checkpoint files after a successful run: if TRUE they are left in checkpoint_dir; if FALSE they are deleted once the combined result is returned. Independent of checkpoint_resume.

log_file

Optional path to a log file. Used whenever checkpointing engages: when checkpoint_dir is set, or under the default checkpoint = TRUE when the data has more than checkpoint_size subjects. Progress messages are always written to the console (unless quietly); if provided, they are also appended here so a colleague can monitor a long run remotely. The log file is safe to read while the run is in progress.

.checkpoint_driven

Internal. Set to TRUE by the internal checkpoint runner so that the per-checkpoint header, banner, and elapsed-time framing are printed by the checkpoint wrapper instead of here (this call then prints only its milestone lines). Not for direct use.

...

Not used. Present so that an argument removed since growthcleanr 2.x (for example num.batches or weight_cap) stops with what to use instead; any other unrecognized argument stops as usual. The full list is in "Removed and renamed arguments" in vignette("experienced-start-here").

Value

By default, a data.table in long format (one row per input measurement, in the same order as the input); the exclusion codes are in its exclude column. (Prior versions returned a character vector of exclusion codes.) Eight columns are always present, plus unit_error_range unless you turn it off:

id

User-provided row identifier (or the auto-generated 1:N if none was usable).

subjid

Subject identifier, as submitted.

param

Measurement parameter, as submitted.

agedays

Age in days, as submitted.

sex

Sex, as submitted.

measurement

Measured value, as submitted.

exclude

The result (a factor): "Include" or a Summary-level exclusion code naming why the value was set aside.

bin_exclude

A two-way collapse of exclude (character): "Include" or "Exclude".

unit_error_range

On by default (set unit_error_range = FALSE to omit). A logical informational flag, TRUE for a value whose magnitude looks like a unit-conversion error; never affects exclude.

mean_ht

Returned by default when the data has adult rows (set mean_ht = FALSE to omit). The adult algorithm's calculated mean height (cm), computed from included heights only and populated on all of a subject's adult height rows; NA for child rows, adult weight rows, and subjects with no included adult height.

Exclusion codes changed in version 3; for the mapping from 2.x codes, see "Mapping from prior exclusion codes" in vignette("experienced-start-here").

Output fidelity. The five echoed input columns (subjid, param, agedays, sex, measurement) carry your verbatim submitted values – growthcleanr never silently alters or drops an input value. For example, imperial values are returned as submitted (not converted to metric), even though internally, growthcleanr converts them to metric. A value growthcleanr cannot use – an uninterpretable sex; a 0, negative, or missing measurement; a missing param; or a negative/NA agedays – is flagged Exclude-Missing-Info; a param that is not one growthcleanr recognizes is flagged Exclude-Not-GC-Param; and a head-circumference value at 5 years or older (beyond the reference) is flagged Exclude-HC-Out-of-Range. In every case the value is still returned as submitted. The internal working values are available via internal_detail/debug (see below).

Column naming. The six data columns (id, subjid, param, agedays, sex, measurement) are renamed to match your original argument expressions when those resolve to a simple name – e.g. cleangrowth(subjid = dt$patid, ...) returns a column named patid. Complex expressions fall back to the canonical name. In data-frame style, output columns keep your column names (e.g. subjid = "patid" returns patid).

Optional columns. Each of these switches adds columns; all default to off unless noted:

exclude_detail

exclude_detailed – the step-level (Detailed) exclusion code behind each Summary exclude value.

tri_exclude

tri_exclude – "Include", "Same-Day", or "Exclude".

cf_detail

cf_status, cf_deltaz, cf_nextz, and three carried-forward design aids (imperial, cf_dage_orig, cf_dage_next).

corr_detail

corr_val (per value) and corr_pt (per subject) gestational-age correction status.

recenter_detail

The recentered CSD z-score columns tbc.sd, ctbc.sd, and rcmedian.sd (child rows; NA for adults) – specialized output for a related tool in development.

internal_detail

growthcleanr's working values for your inputs: gc_internal_meas, gc_internal_param, gc_internal_sex, gc_internal_id, gc_internal_agedays (the whole-day age used for cleaning) (and parsed gc_internal_dob/gc_internal_visit_date if dates were supplied).

display_gc_id

gc_internal_id – the id growthcleanr actually used internally.

debug

Intermediate z-score diagnostics for child rows (sd.orig, sd.corr, tbc.sd, ctbc.sd, and the plus/minus perturbation z-scores) plus gc_internal_sex; for development, not routine use.

qm_detail

Ten per-step child eligibility flags (qm_elig_*); for eligibility-normalized quality measures used for a related package in development. Must be requested explicitly – not turned on by full_detail.

full_detail

Convenience switch turning on all of the above except qm_detail (and independent of unit_error_range).

Non-long output. With output_format = "semi_wide" or "wide" the returned object is your submitted table with the columns named in widened_emit inserted beside the value they describe (see output_format).

The full catalog of exclusion codes (child + adult, Summary and Detailed) is in vignette("exclusion-codes").

Details

Calling styles:

  1. Data-frame style (recommended). Pass a single data.frame or data.table as data. The subjid, param, agedays, sex, measurement, and id arguments are then column-name strings identifying which columns in data to use. Each defaults to the canonical name (e.g. "subjid"), so if your columns already use those names you can just call cleangrowth(data = my_df). Use the column-name arguments only to remap (e.g. subjid = "patid").

  2. Vector style (legacy). Omit data and pass each of subjid, param, agedays, sex, and measurement as a vector. Retained for backward compatibility with existing code; new code should use the data-frame style.

All vectors (or the columns referenced in data) must have the same length and be aligned row-for-row. Pulling values from different datasets is not supported and not checked for.

Arguments at a glance. The many arguments fall into groups; most runs touch only the first one or two:

  • Core input column names – data, subjid, sex, agedays, param, measurement, id.

  • Age from dates (instead of agedays) – dob, visit_date, age_source, date_order.

  • Sex and parameter coding – sex_coding, param_coding.

  • Input/output shape – input_format, output_format, semiwide_cols, wide_cols, max_blocks, widened_emit, carry_through.

  • Run control and performance – parallel, cores, batch_size, quietly, verbose, ref_tables, ref.data.path, log.path.

  • Checkpointed (resumable) runs – checkpoint, checkpoint_dir, checkpoint_size, checkpoint_resume, keep_checkpoints, log_file.

  • Adult algorithm – adult_cutpoint, adult_permissiveness, adult_scale_max_lbs, adult_overrides.

  • EWMA window (child and adult) – ewma_window.

  • Length vs. height handling – length.adjust.

  • Recentering – sd.recenter.

  • Carried-forward rescue – cf_rescue.

  • Optional output columns – exclude_detail, unit_error_range, tri_exclude, cf_detail, corr_detail, recenter_detail, internal_detail, display_gc_id, mean_ht, full_detail, qm_detail, debug.

  • Advanced threshold overrides (rarely changed) – piv.z.*, error.load.*. See vignette("algorithm-functions") for the CSD z-scores (sd.orig) the piv.z.* cutoffs apply to.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Check your setup on a sample of your data first: gc_runtrial(syngrowth)

# Data-frame style (recommended): canonical column names, just pass the
# data.frame.
# syngrowth is a small example dataset bundled with growthcleanr.
df_stats <- as.data.frame(syngrowth)
# Use 5 subjects so the example runs quickly
df_stats <- df_stats[df_stats$subjid %in% unique(df_stats[, "subjid"])[1:5], ]
# We recommend including a unique per-row `id` column (syngrowth already
# does; this shows how to add one)
df_stats$id <- seq_len(nrow(df_stats))
clean_stats <- cleangrowth(data = df_stats)
#> [14:11:54] growthcleanr: cleaning in progress — 5 subjects, 93 measurements, 1 batch of up to 5,000 subjects
#> ************************************************************
#> growthcleanr cleaning summary  (93 measurements)
#>   Weight      : 45 included (80.4%), 11 excluded (19.6%)
#>   Height      : 32 included (86.5%), 5 excluded (13.5%)
#>   Set aside   : 0 (0.0%)
#> ************************************************************

# How many values were included, and why the others were excluded:
table(clean_stats$exclude)
#> 
#>                 Include    Exclude-Not-GC-Param    Exclude-Missing-Info 
#>                      77                       0                       0 
#> Exclude-HC-Out-of-Range       Exclude-Identical      Exclude-Extraneous 
#>                       0                       2                      11 
#>      Exclude-Hard-Limit              Exclude-CF       Exclude-Scale-Max 
#>                       0                       2                       0 
#>         Exclude-Extreme         Exclude-Pattern            Exclude-Pair 
#>                       0                       1                       0 
#>          Exclude-Single     Exclude-Traj-Uneval 
#>                       0                       0 

# The result is your data with an added `exclude` column; keep only the
# measurements growthcleanr says to include:
clean_only <- clean_stats[clean_stats$exclude == "Include", ]

# Data-frame style with remapped column names
my_df <- df_stats
names(my_df)[names(my_df) == "subjid"] <- "patid"
clean_stats <- cleangrowth(data = my_df, subjid = "patid")
#> [14:11:56] growthcleanr: cleaning in progress — 5 subjects, 93 measurements, 1 batch of up to 5,000 subjects
#> ************************************************************
#> growthcleanr cleaning summary  (93 measurements)
#>   Weight      : 45 included (80.4%), 11 excluded (19.6%)
#>   Height      : 32 included (86.5%), 5 excluded (13.5%)
#>   Set aside   : 0 (0.0%)
#> ************************************************************

# Vector style (legacy)
clean_stats <- cleangrowth(subjid = df_stats$subjid,
                           param = df_stats$param,
                           agedays = df_stats$agedays,
                           sex = df_stats$sex,
                           measurement = df_stats$measurement,
                           id = df_stats$id)
#> [14:11:57] growthcleanr: cleaning in progress — 5 subjects, 93 measurements, 1 batch of up to 5,000 subjects
#> ************************************************************
#> growthcleanr cleaning summary  (93 measurements)
#>   Weight      : 45 included (80.4%), 11 excluded (19.6%)
#>   Height      : 32 included (86.5%), 5 excluded (13.5%)
#>   Set aside   : 0 (0.0%)
#> ************************************************************
#> Note: since growthcleanr version 3, cleangrowth() returns a data table (one row per input row), not a vector of exclusion codes. Code written for 2.x that treats the result as a vector (for example sum(result == "Include") or df$gcr_result <- result) can run without an error and give wrong answers; use result$exclude instead. Exclusion codes were also renamed. See 'Updating code written for growthcleanr 2.2.3' in vignette("experienced-start-here"). (Shown once per R session.)

# Parallel processing: run using 2 cores
clean_stats <- cleangrowth(data = df_stats,
                           parallel = TRUE,
                           cores = 2)
#> [14:11:59] growthcleanr: cleaning in progress — 5 subjects, 93 measurements, 1 batch of up to 5,000 subjects
#> ************************************************************
#> growthcleanr cleaning summary  (93 measurements)
#>   Weight      : 45 included (80.4%), 11 excluded (19.6%)
#>   Height      : 32 included (86.5%), 5 excluded (13.5%)
#>   Set aside   : 0 (0.0%)
#> ************************************************************
# }
